name: Benchmark for Reliable Molecular Supervised Learning (Bayesian GNNs)
description: Virtual screening aims to find desirable compounds from chemical library by using computational methods. For this purpose with machine learning, model outputs that can be interpreted as predictive probability will be beneficial, in that a high prediction score corresponds to high probability of correctness. In this work, we present a study on the prediction performance and reliability of graph neural networks trained with the recently proposed Bayesian learning algorithms. Our work shows that Bayesian learning algorithms allow well-calibrated predictions for various GNN architectures and classification tasks. Also, we show the implications of reliable predictions on virtual screening, where Bayesian learning may lead to higher success in finding hit compounds.
evaluation_method: ROC-AUC and calibration metrics (Brier score, ECE); also reports accuracy for classification tasks
reputation: Cited in research on Bayesian GNNs and model calibration for molecular property prediction; moderate recognition within the cheminformatics community.
notes: Non-LLM benchmark focused on small-molecule property prediction; emphasizes calibration (Brier score, ECE) and reliable predictive probabilities. Results can be sensitive to small dataset sizes, class imbalance, and chosen evaluation metric.
